reviews.title: All parents/caretakers need this app!
reviews.contents: As a new mom almost two years ago, I got swept up in researching baby led weaning while pregnant and decided that’s what we were going to do when it was time for my son. Well, by the time my son was 6 months old and ready in February 2020, I got nervous. How do I cut these things for him? Any foods to avoid? Do I have to introduce 1 food at a time for a certain # of days to help show allergies? It doesn’t all have to be mushy/purée food? Even with looking into baby led weaning, I still had so many questions and though I love my pediatrician, they gave such outdated information that I wasn’t sure where to turn! Thankfully I found SolidStarts on Instagram (right when they first started!) and that was the support and guidance I needed this whole time! Save to say, my son will be turning 2 this august and is an AMAZING eater. Every time we go to a family members house, out to eat at a restaurant, or even random social media posts, everyone says how they are amazed with how well he eats and I have to give a big THANK YOU to Jenny and all of the team at Solid Starts because this mama would’ve been so lost and confused without all of their information and support! I highly recommend not only this app but checking out their Instagram page too. So many helpful tips and advice and seeing real babies with how and what they are eating. Thank you again Solid Starts! I’ve got one HAPPY eater!

reviews.title: All mamas need this!
reviews.contents: As a first time mama, I had fed my son too many purees at first and when it was time to feed him solid foods, I wouldn’t feed him much of a variety because he would try something and act like he didn’t like it so I would just think to myself, “Okay. He doesn’t like that. I’m not going to serve it again.” This led to him being picky and not really willing to try new foods. I wouldn’t say that he’s extremely picky, but still.. I knew that I wanted to do something completely different the second time around. As a second time mama, I decided to go with baby led weaning. I knew that I was going to do it, even if I didn’t know how. Right as I was having my second child start solids, I found solid starts. And thank goodness because it helped me so much. I was able to serve him a variety of foods, have him eat what we ate by learning how to cut it and just make simple modifications like not adding salt or sugar. It was slow in the beginning, mostly because I was always afraid of him choking. But they teach you the difference between choking and gagging as well. And as he for better at eating I became more confident in what I was doing as well. I owe it all to solid starts. I would recommend this app to any of my mama friends or family. So great to see my son eat 3 meals a day at only 10 months old and my first son willing to try new things as well.

reviews.title: MUST HAVE FOR ALL PARENTS
reviews.contents: I’ve used Solidstarts Instagram to learn how to cut foods and recipe ideas. However, the FREE app is beyond convenient to search exactly what you’re trying to serve. I’ve used his app for my first child. He’s now 20 months and thriving with food. He eats what we eat and I owe it all to Solidstarts. My daughter is 7 months and we started solids about a month ago. I’ve since forgotten how to serve a lot of foods for her age range. But then I can easily search the app and see how to cut foods, how to prepare, nutrition facts, history of the food etc. and it’s all backed by specialists, doctors and research. There’s also a free recipe included with each food they have in their system. Which is a win-win. You can decide to purchase a subscription to track foods. Their website also provides even MORE searchable data. They have a very advanced search engine which allows you to look up things like “prevent picky eating”, “baby eating fast” etc. and all the articles will populate on that topic. It’s amazing what this company is doing. I recommend this to all of the parents I know. I can’t thank them enough for their hard work and dedication!!

reviews.title: Helpful information horrible functionality
reviews.contents: The information this app provides is wonderful.  The articles are helpful, the instructions on how to prepare different foods safely give me peace of mind, and the guidance on introducing allergens made it much less scary.  BUT, the functionality of this app is absolute trash.  When I try to add a meal to the tracker, it always logs it for the following day and I have to manually go in and individually change every ingredient to the correct day—it’s infuriating!  The allergen introduction feature also just stopped working for me after pistachio.  Usually when you complete an allergen, the next one pops up for you to start, but the app just stopped working once we hit pistachio.  I hate the meal planning feature, and I dislike that you need to complete these other modules (like dip and bite) before it will give you instructions on the next allergen.  Why can’t I just go into the allergen list, click one, and get the instructions and meals for introducing that allergen??  Logging foods is so annoying that I just stopped using the feature after a few weeks.  I will also say this app is very white and has little to no information on many of the Chinese vegetables we consume.  Lastly, the recipes on the app are not good and I did not enjoy any of the ones we tried that are designed to be shared by the whole family.  TLDR:  useful for allergen introduction (as long as the app is working) and for checking how to safely prepare a food (as long as it’s a mainstream food), and not much else.

reviews.title: Pretty good!
reviews.contents:
I love this app, it has been so helpful in so many ways! My son has a dairy protein allergy and so this app made it easy to keep track of what he had tried for his appointments. I did purchase the 100 dollar add on that goes over the whole plan and 100 foods in 100 days etc and I have to say I looked at it once when I bought it but it was like 200 pages and so I never referred back to it again, with a new baby who had dietary complications I just didn’t have the time to sit down and do it but others may find it helpful! 
The only reason I gave the app 4 stars is because of his allergy, there is no option to modify. So yes he’s tried bagels, and yes he’s had this and that, that may include dairy but I gave him non dairy options or substituted the dairy and it does not have the option to do that. So it looks like I introduced dairy when I had not. Which is fine at this time but then when I do introduce dairy it will get complicated to remember if “this bagel or that bagel” were the ones with the dairy or not. I wish they had a food allergy option. Maybe prompted questions “this item contains dairy, was a substitute made?” and the parent clicks yes and it tracks that. But overall, I use it daily, I’ve kept track of everything he has eaten since he started eating foods and I love having this tool.

reviews.title: Waste of Time
reviews.contents: This app makes you create an account and profile for you and your baby, makes you answer a lot of questions, promises a lot of stuff, and then tells you that you have to pay a monthly or yearly subscription to use pretty much anything on the app. For one, this is ridiculous because you’re only going to use this app for a few months or maybe a year at most and then your baby will be eating regular food exactly how you make it anyway so this app will be useless then so obviously they’re just trying to get you to forget you have the subscription so they can keep taking your money even after you no longer need this app. For two, there is absolutely no reason to make people go through the whole process of creating accounts and profiles when you can do pretty much nothing without paying. Why not just tell people up front that they have to pay? It’s such a waste of time. After going through the account and profile making process, I can’t even mark if my child has tried a food or not without making an account. This app sounds like a great idea but sadly the people who need it most aren’t going to have access to it because the price is ridiculous and you can’t even do basic things without paying for the app. Don’t bother downloading this app. I’m sure there are free apps that will at least let you do the basics of what this app does which is all you need.

reviews.title: Extremely Disappointed
reviews.contents:
I absolutely do not appreciate the snaky way the solid starts team suddenly changed their policy on their food database. I just started solids with my firstborn a month ago and have been using their food database (advertised over and over as always free on their instagram/website) to learn how to cut/prepare food safely for my infant, until suddenly I received a countdown saying I had five free searches left before needing to pay an exorbitant price of $20/month or $100 per year. I immediately went to their instagram, where I was confused by their continued messaging stating the food database would continue to be free even with the rollout of their new app. Today, those comments are mysteriously gone, and have been replaced by stuffy corporate legal messaging stating they needed to make this change to continue to offer quality information to parents. Needless to say, I deleted the app.

Update: I am very pleased to hear that Solid Starts has decided to rollback the update and make the food database free again. I have updated my rating accordingly, as I find the food database to be a great resource for new parents starting solids, and I am glad to see it is no longer held behind a paywall.

reviews.title: So wonderful!!
reviews.contents: I have a 7.5 month old and we’ve been using the starting solids guide for a bout a month now. We started out with lots of resistive foods (chicken drumsticks, mango pits, pineapple cores, etc.), some mashes, and some soft foods that my son could bite pieces off of to further practice chewing and spitting. Oh goodness the gagging was so nerve racking to watch, I hated feeling like my baby was struggling and potentially could choke, but watching stories on the Solid Starts Instagram page and knowing that I had prepared his food properly for his age using this app reassured me to keep pushing through with solids and not be afraid of him gagging - Solid Starts taught me that gagging is part of learning to eat solids and is a protective mechanism (the airway actually closes itself off when baby is gagging, for protection). I have been waiting for things to “click” for my little guy to really engage his chewing skills and not gag as much and last night I gave him a piece of chicken breast (that I was quite nervous about him ripping pieces off of) and he ate it like a champ showing off his freshly learned strong chewing skills and I was so so proud of him!!! It turned out to be the dinner that he has consumed the most so far and the least stressful for me to watch (bc there was significantly less gagging), it was amazing!!! The things I’ve learned from Solid Starts have been the reason I was able to teach my son these skills and to have the confidence as a nervous parent to move forward even when it felt scary! Solid Starts is so wonderful, and this app os extremely helpful, I check it every time before feeding him a new food to make sure I have prepped the size/shape appropriately for his age so that we are as safe as we can be and he can just focus on enjoying his food vs. getting frustrated! ♥️

reviews.title: Inconsistency within the app
reviews.contents: I like the app, but there is room for improvement. Tracking within the app doesn’t always show up in all the different sections of the app. You might track a particular allergen on your “calendar,” showing that the allergen has been introduced, but then it’s listed as “in progress” under the list of allergens (even if you’ve already done the full 1, 2, 3 series introduction for that food). Then other allergens I’ve introduced that only call for being given one time to consider the introduction complete, those don’t show up at all on the list of allergens at all and still say “not started.” Then, sometimes when you track an allergen, the app prompts you to select whether there was a reaction or not, but if you track in a different area of the app, that prompt doesn’t come up. It took me forever to figure out that the only place it will prompt me to select whether there was a reaction is if I track it on the calendar page, not from the meal page. All of these things are annoying. I also feel like I get very little guidance about what my next meals should be or how many meals per week I should be aiming for. I paid for the app and feel frustrated with all these issues.

reviews.title: Removed best feature with update
reviews.contents:
UPDATE: 
Notice how in their copy pasted response to everyone who had a similar recent issue they don’t address the fact that we lost all our progress, that is just gone with this “upgrade.” Nothing they suggest works. There is no “Paths” feature, that word isn't even in the app, same with first bites. Do not waste money on this app if you’re expecting to rely on it to help ease your baby into solids because the developer will just pull the rug on you at any time. They are still selling the PDF of the old content on their website which they link to if you try to get help, probably to try to skirt Apple’s subscription fees. If you have a similar issue with the update I recommend reporting them to Apple for violating their policies. 
ORIGINAL REVIEW: 
The best feature of the subscription was the Compass meal plan which had meals mapped out day by day with what to buy. The app just updated and removed this feature (they call it an “upgraded” Compass) right before our breakfast with no warning. We lost all our progress and no longer have the plan we were relying on for the rest of the week. It seems like they moved this feature to the website subscription which is separate from the app subscription. App subscription is basically worthless now and developer shouldn’t be trusted with your money
